question.text: Per SEBI advertisement guidance referred to in the workbook, how should performance be reported for a scheme that has existed for more than 6 months but less than 1 year?

answer.text: As a simple annualized growth rate for the past 6 months
As an 80% CAGR for the half-year
Past performance must be shown for any period, including under 6 months

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook says that for schemes in existence for more than six months but less than one year, performance advertisements should provide a simple annualized growth rate for the past 6 months. Schemes in existence for less than six months should not provide any past performance figures. The Trap: The workbook's wording is "simple annualized growth rate", not CAGR. Annualizing a short-period return as if it were CAGR overstates expected performance, which is why SEBI's advertisement guidance distinguishes between simple annualization and compounded annualization. Note: When discussing returns with investors, follow the workbook's distinction between simple annualization (under 1 year) and CAGR (1 year and above) and avoid mixing the two.
